content.body_data: Alice 3: Fair: formatters can enforce either. But accessibility is better served by editor-side tooling, like tab-width rendering or screen-reader settings, than by repo policy. Spaces avoid tool-specific breakage in diffs, terminals, and patches. Bob, is flexible width worth that portability cost?

content.body_data: Bob 3: Across heterogeneous viewers, portability can outweigh flexible width; editor tooling can help, though it cannot universally reinterpret space indentation. Tabs remain attractive in controlled toolchains. My remaining concern is migration churn: should our recommendation preserve established repository conventions rather than reformat existing code?

summary.author: sjnnUlhXM
summary.preview_data: Shared recommendation: Use spaces for portability and predictable diffs, enforced by formatter and CI. Tradeoff: lose per-reader indentation width. Preserve an existing repository convention rather than reformat it; apply spaces by default to new projects.
